bottleneck: Gut microbes correlate with depression, Parkinson's, and autism in study after study, but causality is unproven: do microbes drive brain changes, or do brain-driven diet and lifestyle changes alter the microbes? Fecal transplant and probiotic trials show inconsistent hints, yet no specific microbial mechanism — metabolite, immune signal, or vagal pathway — is validated as a therapeutic lever in humans. The microbiome's sheer complexity (trillions of organisms, thousands of metabolites) defeats the reductionist experiments that established causality elsewhere. The axis is real; its direction and levers are not.
current_state: Probiotic and FMT trials for brain disorders show inconsistent results. No gut-brain therapy is approved for any neurological or psychiatric indication.
title: Gut-brain causality unproven in humans
why_it_blocks: A causal gut-brain lever would open entirely new psychiatric treatments — potentially safer than brain-penetrating drugs. Without causality, the field sells correlation as therapy and patients experiment on themselves.
